look_here_first: Look closely at one apparent windmill: three separate asymmetric flowers open together within three involucral bracts. Then inspect a mature winged anthocarp and its glands to separate Allionia incarnata from A. choisyi.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Trailing branched stems with paired unequal leaves.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Three simultaneously open asymmetric flowers make one flower-like display.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature fruiting perianth (anthocarp) has five ribs, wings and glands; inspect both surfaces.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Trailing or spreading herb; the selected photo shows stems against the ground, leaves and several flowering units.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite leaves in unequal pairs; close node photo still needed.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Each apparent flower-like unit comprises three separate asymmetric flowers with three involucral bracts.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Winged/glandular five-ribbed anthocarp, typically 2.9–4.7 mm in the existing review, variable.

key_traits.label: Lookalike separators
key_traits.text: Allionia choisyi requires mature fruit convexity, rib and gland-pattern comparison. Magenta color alone is inadequate. Varieties of A. incarnata overlap in dimensions; no variety assigned from source-only name or this habit photograph.
